title: introduce-enclave-backed-kms-proxy-and-masked-audit-indexer
author: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Adds an enclave-backed KMS proxy component and a masked-audit-indexer to satisfy customer compliance requirements around key locality, non-repudiable audit proofs, and PII-minimized audit searchability. Motivation: Some regulated customers require KMS operations to be provably executed inside a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) and audit logs to avoid storing raw PII while remaining searchable for incident investigations. This change provides an optional, opt-in path that can be enabled per-tenant and tied to RBAC v2 attributes.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces services/kms/enclave_proxy which forwards KMS encrypt/decrypt/sign calls through a small TEE shim. The shim adds a signed KMS usage attestation that includes region and enclave nonce.
- Adds a masked-audit-indexer that consumes audit events, strips or tokenizes PII fields (email, full text prompts), and stores cryptographic fingerprints plus minimal context for fast search. Raw sealed audit blobs are still retained behind customer KMS.
- Extends RBAC v2 schema with a new boolean operator attribute `enclave_allowed` and a policy evaluator that denies KMS-proxied operations when the attribute is false.
- Wiring: feature flag `enclave_kms.enabled` and tenant-level config `kms.enclave_mode: "required|preferred|disabled"`.
- Adds integration tests and a small health-check endpoint for the enclave proxy.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests for attribute evaluator and indexer masking rules
- [x] Integration test exercising end-to-end KMS request with attestation header
- [x] Metrics and tracing for proxy latency and indexer processing
- [x] Docs: compliance/enclave-kms.md and operator guide
- [x] Migration plan for existing audit retention (sealed blobs unaffected)

Risk notes: The enclave proxy changes request paths for KMS operations. We made the proxy pluggable and default-off per-tenant. There is an automatic fallback to standard KMS path when attestation verification fails for operator-initiated test calls (controlled by feature flag during rollout). Performance impact is about +6-12ms median for KMS calls in our canary hardware profiles; indexer adds async processing but does not affect request latency.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy code to staging with feature flag off.
2) Enable for internal test tenant and run workload generator for 48h.
3) Canary to 5% of EU tenants that requested enclave verification.
4) Gradual percentage increase with telemetry checks: attestation success rate, proxy error rate, indexer backpressure.

Backward compatibility: No API-breaking changes. Existing tenants can continue to use KMS without enabling enclave mode. RBAC v2 policy additions are additive; policies without `enclave_allowed` default to false for the stricter enforcement path.

Notes about audit search: The masked indexer stores HMACed fingerprints (tenant-scoped) so that investigators can match search terms without storing raw PII. Raw events are sealed with tenant CMK and kept in cold storage for forensic needs, accessible only with an elevated approval flow described in docs.

Related: ENG-2301 (design doc), SEC-412 (threat model), SUP-783 (customer request ticket).

Commit summary: see `commits` field for individual messages.

Merge: Squash-merged after CI fixed a flaky integration test (see review thread).

release_notes: Add optional enclave-backed KMS proxy (opt-in per-tenant) and masked audit indexer to support TEE-attested key usage and PII-reduced searchable audit traces. Comes with RBAC v2 attribute `enclave_allowed` and tenant-level `kms.enclave_mode` config. Rollout controlled by feature flag.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: proxy path could introduce latency or transient KMS failures. Mitigation: feature-flagged rollout, fail-open toggle for non-production tenants, circuit breaker, detailed telemetry and automatic rollback on elevated error rates.
